published_source: Shown only in Figure 3 of the published article (papers/mnsc/mnsc.2025.02515.pdf); no printed value. Authors' code output recorded in authors_code_* (ruling (t) convention, applied Nov 4 2026). Earlier: Authors' code.R re-run on the package data: did::att_gt (dr, notyettreated, varying base period, weights num_individs_2015, cluster county) + aggte(type = 'dynamic', min_e = -8, max_e = 16); published_coef is the dynamic overall ATT (equal-weight average of horizons 0..16), SE analytical (bstrap = FALSE). The article shows the horizon path as a figure; the path from the re-run is in ~/did_packages/_work/mnsc.2025.02515/verify_authors_es_paths.csv. Nov 2: the article (data/text/mnsc/mnsc.2025.02515.txt) shows the path graphically only (Figure 3(d)) over -8..16 quarters; no printed coefficients, so the code re-run is the published reference.
replication_status: exact_code_rerun (figure values not printed; window and outcome verified against the article)
notes: General Access design: gvar first_treat_time = quarter of first legal sports betting (retail or online; 0 = never). All 3,108 counties in final-reg-data.csv, quarters 1-30. 13 adoption cohorts (quarters 10,11,12,15,16,17,18,20,21,23,24,27,29); 1,269 never-treated counties; no always-treated counties. Event study: authors' aggte(type = 'dynamic', min_e = -8, max_e = 16) with varying base period; pipeline uses universal base period (identical post-period coefficients, pre-period coefficients differ in definition). published_coef is the authors' dynamic overall ATT (equal-weight average of horizons 0..16), which is the quantity the pipeline's CSA post-average targets. Authors report Callaway-Sant'Anna (did::att_gt, control_group = 'notyettreated', est_method = 'dr', base_period = 'varying', allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE, xformla = ~1, weightsname = 'num_individs_2015', clustervars = county, bstrap = TRUE without a seed). No TWFE regression exists in the package; the TWFE counterpart is D = 1[gvar > 0 & time >= gvar] with county FE + quarter FE, weights num_individs_2015, clustered by county. Treatment never switches off (defined from a unit-constant timing variable). Outcome levels were additively transformed by the authors to hide actual levels (README); county IDs anonymized; underlying UC Consumer Credit Panel is restricted. published_coef/published_se are the authors' code re-run on the package data (CSA point estimate, deterministic; analytical SE from bstrap = FALSE): the article (text now in data/text/mnsc/) plots this path without printing coefficients (Nov 2 check). Project member Davide Proserpio is a coauthor (PROTOCOL Section 6).

event_structure.source: code.R line 237 (did::att_gt, control_group notyettreated, est_method dr, base_period varying, allow_unbalanced_panel TRUE, weights num_individs_2015, cluster county) and lines 656-664 (aggte type 'dynamic', min_e = -8, max_e = 16); article Section 5: 'event studies and ATTs covering 8 quarters before and 16 quarters after the policy'. Event time e = time - first_treat_time (quarters); time is consecutive in the sample (1..30), so e = rel = t - g in the pipeline index. Callaway-Sant'Anna path: single-quarter bins -8..16 as reported, reference -1 (universal base; the authors' varying base changes only the pre-period definition). Relative times outside the window get open endpoint bins (<= -9, >= 17), estimated but not summarized, so no treated row is uncovered: did keeps those rows and computes their cells (early pre-periods of late cohorts are not-yet-treated controls for earlier cohorts), so 'drop' would change the published path, and pooling them with the reference would subtract their effects from every CS bin. No authors' TWFE exists; the TWFE counterpart estimates the same bins.
event_structure.verified: did 2.5.1 on the authors' sample (verify_authors_csa.R): universal-base (pipeline) dynamic estimates for e = 0..16 equal the authors' varying-base path, max abs diff 2.9e-16; their equal-weight mean equals published_coef (the authors' dynamic overall ATT, e = 0..16) to 2.9e-17. es_parse/es_assign checked on the pipeline sample (nov2_check_02515.R): no uncovered treated rows.

csa_weights_note: Nov 2: the published CSA comes from R did (or staggered, whose estimates did reproduces), which weights cells by fixed cohort shares; Hull's DiD-averaging weights cells by treated-observation counts. 'did' reproduces the published number (main analysis, option B); the strict-Hull run (CSA_STRICT_HULL=1, option A) ignores this field.
